questions.prompt: Ten identical blocks are better than one repeat block.

learn.intro: Programmers are lazy — in a good way! Today we meet a block that repeats for us.

slides.text: To walk 10 steps 10 times you don't need 10 identical blocks. There is a **repeat** block — like a bracket: everything inside repeats.
Like squats in PE: "repeat 10 times — squat". Add "wait 0.2 seconds" — the cat walks smoothly instead of jumping.

check.prompt: Why do we need the repeat block?
options: To avoid lots of identical blocks

slides.text: The **Costumes** tab: the cat has two costumes — two pictures with legs in different positions. Switch them fast and it looks like walking. That is how cartoons are made!
slides.code:
when green flag clicked
repeat 10
    move 10 steps
    next costume
    wait 0.2 seconds

check.prompt: Switching costumes fast makes the cat look like it walks.

slides.text: "Repeat 10" → **"forever"**. The cat walks off the edge → add **"if on edge, bounce"**. Now it walks back and forth.
So the cat doesn't walk upside down — the block "set rotation style: left-right".

check.prompt: Which block keeps the cat from leaving the edge?
